_comment: Two rules are switched off here. Neither is a silent suppression: both carry a reason and a test that holds the underlying property.

_why.bootstrap.cp-authorization: False positive, verified. The rule greps each CP controller for `$this->authorize(`, `Gate::`, `->can(`, `abort_unless`, `abort_if` or `authorizeResource`. This addon guards through `Cp\Controller::authorizeOrFail()` (src/Http/Controllers/Cp/Controller.php:21), which the rule's pattern list does not know — the base class deliberately routes through Laravel's Gate rather than Statamic's `hasPermission()`, because the latter crashes on eloquent-driver sites where the authenticated model is a plain App\Models\User. `ExportController::store()` calls it on its first line (src/Http/Controllers/Cp/ExportController.php:16). The property the rule is protecting is held by a test, not by this suppression: tests/Feature/CpWriteRouteAuthorizationTest.php walks the router, picks every POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE route in the leadhub namespace with all feature flags on, and asserts each answers 403 to a CP user without LeadHub permissions. All 38 do. A new unguarded write route fails there on the day it is added.
_why.testing.addon-testcase: Deliberate, and it needs a decision rather than a quiet fix. Switching tests/TestCase.php to Statamic\Testing\AddonTestCase was attempted on 2026-08-01 and produced 201 failures out of 501. AddonTestCase mocks the Nav facade without an `extend` expectation, and — more fundamentally — its manifest wiring makes Statamic register the addon's own routes and listeners on top of the ones this TestCase mounts by hand, so every event-driven side effect fires twice (engagement scores came out doubled). The hand-rolled setup is not accidental: it boots the brand-context sibling before this addon, flips the storage driver from LEADHUB_DRIVER, swaps SQLite for MySQL from DB_DRIVER for the InnoDB key-length suite, purges the flat-file store between tests, and mounts the CP routes with SubstituteBindings so a sibling addon's Route::bind() collision is reproducible. Migrating to AddonTestCase means rebuilding all of that against core's ordering — a project, not a sweep item. Tracked for a separate pass.
